memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then God said to Jacob, 'Go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau.'" - Gen 35:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the tragedy at Shechem, God speaks again to Jacob with a gracious command: "Go up to Bethel and settle there." Bethel was where it had all begun — the place where God had first met Jacob years ago, the lonely fugitive with a stone for a pillow. Now God calls him back to that place of first encounter, the place where he had made his vow.

There is real grace in this call. Jacob had drifted. He had settled at Shechem instead of going all the way to Bethel, and the results had been disastrous. Yet God does not abandon him. Instead, He calls him to return — to go back to the place of first devotion and begin again.

God often does this with us. When we have wandered, settled for less, or let our devotion grow cold, He graciously calls us back to our "Bethel" — back to the place where we first met Him, first trusted Him, first gave ourselves to Him. The risen Christ said to a drifting church, "Remember the height from which you have fallen! Repent and do the things you did at first" (Rev 2:5).

Is God calling you back to your Bethel? Back to prayer, to His Word, to the wholehearted devotion you once had? His call to return is always a call of grace. Answer it, and go up to Bethel.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I drifted from my first devotion to God?
2. Is God calling me back to my "Bethel"?
3. What would it mean to return to Him wholeheartedly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that when I drift, You graciously call me back. Draw me to my Bethel — to the wholehearted devotion I first had for You. I want to return to You. Amen.
